지문 설계: 근거 위치 — 앞: 화자의 말투(불평·농담) / 중간: 자기 정정·망설임 어구 / 뒤: 화자가 조용히 해 주는 행동 또는 피하는 화제. 직접 서술 금지 — 화자의 직접 평가어(admire, resent, grateful 등)와 '마음'을 말하는 문장 금지.

previous.passage: I run a spice shop in Marrakesh that a former ship's cook built to look like a galley, all brass hooks and low beams, and every morning Joaquin ducks under those beams to complain about my saffron. Too damp, too pale, too expensive. He has said this for nine years. He buys a gram each time anyway, counted out of a jar he insists I lift down from the top shelf. Last month a hotel offered to buy my stock and the lease; I could retire to my daughter's house in Fes. I told Joaquin, mostly to watch his face. He said good, the hotel's saffron would at least be dry. I am not saying I was hurt, exactly. I signed nothing that week. I did move the jar to the lowest shelf, where a man with a bad back could reach it himself, and I wrote the price on the lid in larger numbers.
previous.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Joaquin?
options: Weary irritation at his complaints while hoping the sale will put an end to them
Real fondness for him while feeling guilty about nearly selling the shop
Protective care for him while keeping up a show of mutual grumbling
Proud attachment to the galley shop while doubting its worth to customers
previous.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 Joaquin의 불평을 건조하게 옮기고 그의 반응을 보려고 매각 이야기를 꺼내는 등 서로 투덜대는 말투를 유지한다. 중간의 'not saying I was hurt, exactly'라는 망설이는 정정은 그 말투 아래 감정이 있음을 암시한다. 뒤에서 화자는 아무것도 서명하지 않고, 허리가 아픈 Joaquin이 직접 닿도록 병을 아래 칸으로 옮기며 가격을 크게 적는데, 이는 그를 배려하는 행동이다. 따라서 C가 정답이며, A는 말투만 읽었고, B는 배려의 이유를 죄책감으로 바꾸었으며, D는 지문의 가게 묘사를 빌려 태도로 일반화했다.

Two rules for the crossing at the dry riverbed in Vermont:
step on the flat stones, and do not mention the trial.
Solange, retired from the bench, keeps the first rule loudly;
she lectures me on stones the way she once lectured juries,
and I roll my eyes behind her, as clerks are allowed to do.
Her rulings ran long. So do her walks.
I would not call this friendship, exactly.
The second rule we keep without a word.
Last week, halfway across, she slowed
where the old flood line still stains the bank,
the place where the case began.
I started talking about stones,
the gray ones, the split ones, the one shaped like a gavel,
and kept on talking until we reached the far side,
and offered my arm for the climb, which she took.
